what-is-a-discovery-call.0: New to sales, or moving from a non-sales role? Then "discovery call" can sound like jargon. Really it is just the meeting where you listen more than you talk, and a good discovery call saves both sides time: the buyer gets understood, and you find out whether a deal is real.
what-is-a-discovery-call.1: Below: the purpose of a discovery call, how long it should be, a simple agenda and script, 25 questions to ask, and how to follow up.
what-is-a-discovery-call.2: In sales, a discovery call is the first meeting after a prospect shows interest, where the seller asks questions to understand the buyer's situation and qualify the opportunity. Demo or proposal comes later ([Vidyard's sales glossary](https://www.vidyard.com/glossary/sales-glossary-discovery-call/) defines it the same way). [Salesforce](https://www.salesforce.com/blog/sales/what-is-a-discovery-call/) and most sales methodologies treat it as the foundation of the deal.
what-is-a-discovery-call.5: Many teams use frameworks such as BANT (budget, authority, need, timeline) or MEDDIC to structure these questions. Covering all 4 areas matters more than which framework you pick.

what-is-a-discovery-call.9: Ask open questions that start with what, how and why. Below are 25 discovery call questions grouped by purpose. Pick 8 to 10 per call.
what-is-a-discovery-call.10: Discovery calls are important because they decide whether the rest of the sales process is worth anyone's time. Done well, one qualifies out bad-fit deals early, gives you the buyer's own words for later proposals, and makes the demo shorter and more relevant.
what-is-a-discovery-call.11: They also build trust. Buyers who feel understood on the first call are far more likely to take the second one, which is why many sales teams treat discovery quality as a leading indicator of win rate.
what-is-a-discovery-call.12: A cold call is an unscheduled first contact to earn a conversation, while a discovery call is a scheduled conversation with someone who already agreed to talk. Their goals differ:
what-is-a-discovery-call.16: A discovery call is for listening and qualifying; a demo is for showing how your product solves the problems you uncovered. Built on good discovery, demos are shorter and more relevant. Why? You show only what matters to that buyer.
what-is-a-discovery-call.18: Same structure everywhere: understand the situation, the problem and the goal, then agree on a next step.
what-is-a-discovery-call.20: More on sales tooling: our guide to [sales conversation intelligence](https://lynkk.ai/blog/sales-conversation-intelligence).
what-is-a-discovery-call.22: In a good recap, include the prospect's top goal, main challenge and timeline in their own words, then the date of the next meeting. Example 2 in our [follow-up email after meeting](https://lynkk.ai/blog/follow-up-email-after-meeting) guide shows one.
what-is-a-discovery-call.25: Not exactly. Think two-way conversation. While the seller asks most of the questions, the buyer should also learn something useful and decide whether to continue, leaving with a clearer view of their own problem and options. Good calls feel useful to the buyer.
what-is-a-discovery-call.27: After the call, the seller sends a recap and, if there is a fit, books the next step, often a demo with additional stakeholders or a proposal review. Send that recap the same day, using the prospect's own words for their goals, challenges and timeline.
what-is-a-discovery-call.28: You may also hear it called a discovery meeting, a qualification call, a needs analysis call or, for consultants and coaches, a consultation call. Whatever the name, the structure is the same: understand the situation, the problem and the goal, then agree on a next step.
